newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB shares jump for second day.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB shares jump for second day.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc rose for a second day on Tuesday as Monday's reports of plans to push ahead with digital TV, and positive regulatory news, brought buyers back into the stock, traders said.
The stock was up 28p at 517-1/2 by 1040 GMT in active trading of 2.6 million shares.
After reaching a record 698p in October, BSkyB shares tumbled to a five-month low of 473p on December 13 amid growing competition worries.
"The stock has had a massive tumble so it's no surprise it has bounced," said one market-maker.
BSkyB yesterday cleared a key regulatory hurdle as the Office of Fair Trading said it had accepted the company's terms for the supply of its channels to cable operators.
Separately, a report in the Financial Times said BSkyB would shortly press ahead with a decoder box for new channels plus pay-per-view sport and movies.
Tuesday's gain came despite a report in the FT that cable companies were considering a legal challenge to the charges BSkyB sets for carrying other TV programmes.
